original.target_description: Study 4: low versus high self-concept clarity, retention choice between The Economist and People subscriptions; relative preference for the identity-relevant subscription. Only n_o assigned.

n.sample_role: Participants in the retention-choice comparison; retention-specific analytic count not reported. The printed 405 is the whole Study 4 completion count across retention and acquisition conditions.
n.exclusions: No exclusions or final retention-condition cell counts documented in the supplied Study 4 section.
n.location: Published p. 896 (PDF page 10), Study 4 Method: Participants and Procedure; Results and Discussion; Figure 4
n.quote:
Four hundred five people from MTurk
completed the study ... Among participants who made a retention choice, ... those in the low SCC condition were more likely to retain ... the identity-relevant subscription than those in the high ... SCC condition

notes: Only n_o assigned; all other fields are placeholders. Study 4 is identified by the study number, subscription-retention outcome and low/high SCC manipulation. The source reports 405 completed participants across a 2 x 2 between-subjects design, with retention and acquisition as separate choice conditions. It reports a retention simple-effect test using F(1, 401), but gives neither retention-group counts nor an explicit analytic N for that contrast. Whole-study N=405 retained only as a candidate common-model count, not substituted for retention analytic N. No N inferred from degrees of freedom and no arithmetic performed. The supplied locator p. 29 does not match the published pagination; Study 4 is on published pp. 895–896. PDF page 10 rendered and inspected.
